AL.lo: Occupational license taxes in some cities/counties, typically 0.5%-2% of wages (e.g., Birmingham 1%, Gadsden 2%); TF avg local burden 0.07% of AGI.
AL.no: Federal income tax paid is deductible on the Alabama return. OBBBA: Alabama did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions but created its own overtime premium deduction: lesser of the overtime premium or $1,000 per taxpayer, tax years 2026-2028 (Act 2026-604). Phases down with AGI: single $3,000 at AGI <= $25,499, reduced $25 per $500 of AGI above, minimum $2,500; MFJ $8,500 at AGI <= $25,999, reduced $175 per $500, minimum $5,000. Dependent exemption $1,000 if AGI <= $50,000; $500 for $50,001-$100,000; $300 above $100,000 (TF footnote c).

AZ.no: Flat tax. OBBBA: HB 4168 updated IRC conformity to Jan 1, 2026 and created subtractions for federal qualified tips (IRC 224), qualified overtime (IRC 225) and the senior deduction, effective from TY2025 (decoupled from bonus depreciation). HB 4168 (signed June 13, 2026) sets the TY2026 standard deduction at $15,750 single/MFS, $23,625 HOH, $31,500 MFJ, plus an add-on equal to charitable contributions capped at $1,000 single/$2,000 MFJ. (TF's Feb-2026 table showed $8,350/$16,700 on pre-OBBBA conformity; superseded.) No personal exemption. Dependent tax credit $125 per dependent under 17 (raised from $100 by HB 4168 for TY2026) and $25 per dependent 17+; phases out above federal AGI $200,000 single / $400,000 MFJ.

AR.no: Brackets shown are the table for net taxable income up to $94,700 (same for all filing statuses; thresholds from 2026 DFA formula). Above $94,700 a separate table applies: 2% on the first $4,700 and 3.7% on the rest, with a bracket-adjustment deduction for net income $94,701-$97,600. Top rate cut to 3.7% retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 by HB 1001/SB 1 (Acts 1-2 of the 2026 extraordinary session, signed May 2026); revised tables are inflation indexed. TF's Feb-2026 table (3.9%, $4,600/$92,300 thresholds) is superseded. $2,470 per taxpayer (2026 DFA withholding formula). Personal tax credit $29 per taxpayer and per dependent.

CA.lo: No local tax on wages (San Francisco/Los Angeles levy business/payroll taxes on employers).
CA.no: Brackets are 2025 inflation-indexed amounts (TF footnote j; 2026 indexing not published); these are also used in EDD's 2026 withholding schedules. 13.3% top rate includes the 1% Mental Health Services Tax on taxable income over $1,000,000 for all filers (hence the MFJ 12.3% step at $1,000,000). Employee SDI payroll tax (no wage cap) is separate. OBBBA: California did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger). 2025 amounts (FTB); 2026 indexed amounts not yet published. TF's table showed $5,540/$11,080 (the 2024 amounts). 2025 exemption credits from Form 540 ($153 personal, $475 per dependent); 2026 indexed amounts not yet published. Credits phase out by $6 (single) / $12 (MFJ) per $2,500 of federal AGI above $252,203 / $504,411 (2025).

CO.lo: Occupational privilege taxes (flat monthly amounts) in a few cities, e.g., Denver $5.75/month employee share, Aurora $2/month.
CO.no: Flat tax. Rate can be temporarily lowered under TABOR-surplus triggers (none reflected for 2026 in TF table). High-AGI taxpayers must add back part of federal std/itemized deductions (thresholds not verified here). OBBBA: requires add-back of the federal overtime deduction from TY2026 (HB 25-1296; a 2025 special-session bill to repeal it was postponed indefinitely); federal tips deduction flows through (Kiplinger). Initiative 195 (Nov 2026 ballot) would create a graduated tax from 2027. Federal standard deduction (Colorado starts from federal taxable income).

CT.no: Phase-out of the 2% bracket and 'tax benefit recapture' make higher-income filers pay effectively higher rates on all income. No standard deduction. Personal exemption reduced $1,000 per $1,000 of CT AGI above $30,000 (single) / $48,000 (MFJ). Also a personal tax credit of 1%-75% of tax for lower AGIs.

DE.no: Same brackets for all filing statuses. $110 personal credit per person.

DC.no: Rates unchanged since 2022 (OTR). OBBBA: DC did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger). Tied to the federal standard deduction (TF).

GA.no: Flat tax. HB 463 (Act 465, signed 2026) cut the rate 5.19% -> 4.99% for tax years beginning Jan 1, 2026, with contingent 0.125-pt annual cuts toward 3.99%. TF's Feb-2026 table (5.19%, $12k/$24k, $4k) is superseded. OBBBA: partial conformity - Georgia excludes up to $1,750 of overtime pay (full-time hourly workers) and up to $1,750 of cash tips, tax years 2026-2028. Raised from $12,000/$24,000 by HB 463 for 2026 (HOH and MFS $15,000). No personal exemption; dependent deduction $5,000 for 2026 (was $4,000) per GA DOR 2026 Employer's Tax Guide and Plante Moran.

HI.no: 2026 brackets are the same as 2025 under Act 46. Act 24 of 2026 (SB 3125) adds a 13% top rate (over $500k single / $1M MFJ) starting TY2027 - not in effect for 2026. Act 46 (2024) schedule per Hawaii DOTAX Announcement 2024-03: $8,000 single / $12,000 HOH / $16,000 MFJ for 2026-2027 (TF's table showed the 2024-25 amounts $4,400/$8,800). $1,144 per person.

ID.no: Flat 5.3% above a zero bracket; the $4,811/$9,622 zero-bracket amounts are TF's figures (2025 indexed; 2026 indexed amount not confirmed). Rate 5.3% confirmed by the Idaho State Tax Commission July-2026 withholding table. OBBBA: HB 559 (signed Feb 2026) conformed to the federal tips, overtime, senior and car-loan-interest deductions retroactive to Jan 1, 2025. Federal standard deduction amounts (HB 559 adopted the OBBBA standard deduction). No exemptions (Idaho has a child tax credit).

IL.no: Flat tax. OBBBA: Illinois did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger). No standard deduction. Not allowed if AGI exceeds $250,000 (single) / $500,000 (MFJ).

IN.lo: County income taxes on all 92 counties: about 0.5% (Porter) to 3.0% (Randolph); Marion 2.02%, Allen 1.59%, Hamilton 1.1%, Lake 1.5% (DOR Departmental Notice #1, rates eff. Oct 1, 2026).
IN.no: Flat tax; 2.95% for 2026 (DOR), scheduled 2.9% in 2027. OBBBA: SEA 243 (2026) excludes federal qualified tips and overtime (and car-loan interest) from state and local income tax for TY2026 only. No standard deduction. $1,000 per person; qualifying dependent children get an additional $1,500 ($3,000 in the first year for some).

IA.lo: School district income surtaxes (a percentage of state tax set by each district) and the Appanoose County EMS surtax.
IA.no: Flat tax since 2025. OBBBA: federal deductions incl. tips/overtime reportedly flow through via the federal-taxable-income starting point (secondary source only; not confirmed with Iowa DOR). Federal standard deduction (Iowa starts from federal taxable income). $40 personal/dependent credit.

KS.no: SB 269 revenue-trigger rate cuts were NOT triggered for 2026 (KDOR Notice 25-06).

KY.lo: City/county (and some school) occupational license taxes, commonly ~0.5%-2.5% of wages (e.g., Louisville Metro ~2.2% resident / ~1.45% nonresident; Lexington-Fayette 2.25%).
KY.no: Flat tax; 3.5% and $3,360 confirmed by KY DOR 2026 withholding formula. Not doubled for joint returns; spouses filing separately on a combined return can each take $3,360 (so many couples do). No personal exemptions; low-income Family Size Tax Credit.

LA.no: Flat tax since 2025. Inflation indexed. Personal exemptions replaced by the larger standard deduction in the 2025 reform.

ME.no: LD 2212 (approved Apr 9, 2026) adds a 2% surcharge on Maine taxable income over $1,000,000 single / $1,500,000 MFJ, retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 (shown as the 9.15% bracket). OBBBA: Maine did not adopt the federal tips/overtime deductions (Kiplinger). Maine Revenue Services 2026 rate schedules revised May 20, 2026 ($23,550 HOH). Phases out at higher incomes (TF 2025 thresholds: begins over $100,000 single / $200,050 MFJ). TF's table showed $8,350/$16,700; superseded. Personal exemption $5,300 per taxpayer/spouse (phases out at high income). Dependents get a refundable credit ($305 age 6+, $610 under 6 per TF, 2025 amounts), not an exemption.

MD.lo: County/Baltimore City income tax on residents 2.25%-3.30% of MD taxable income for 2026 (e.g., Montgomery/PG/Baltimore City 3.20%, Dorchester and Kent 3.30%, Worcester 2.25%; Anne Arundel and Frederick tiered); nonresident special tax 2.25%. Max allowed rate rose to 3.3% from 2026.
MD.no: 2% surtax on net capital gains for federal AGI over $350,000 (since 2025). Itemized deductions reduced 7.5% of FAGI over $200,000. Flat amount since 2025, indexed to COLA thereafter (2026 indexed figure not separately confirmed; TF shows $3,350/$6,700). Phases out between AGI $100k-$150k (single) / $150k-$200k (married).

MA.no: 5% flat rate plus 4% surtax on income over $1,107,750 for TY2026 (mass.gov; TF showed the 2025 threshold $1,083,150). Same threshold for joint filers. Short-term capital gains 8.5%. Paid family/medical leave payroll contribution is separate. No standard deduction.

MI.lo: 24 cities levy income tax, mostly 1% resident / 0.5% nonresident; Detroit 2.4% / 1.2%, Grand Rapids 1.5% / 0.75%.
MI.no: Flat tax. OBBBA: Public Act 24 of 2025 creates state deductions for qualified overtime and qualified tips mirroring the federal deductions, tax years 2026-2028 (Treasury notice Jan 6, 2026). No standard deduction.

MN.no: 1% surtax on net investment income over $1 million. State-set amount (MN DOR 2026). Reduced for high AGI (TF: 3% of AGI over $244,400, 10% over $337,800, max 80% reduction). Dependent exemption only.

MO.lo: Kansas City and St. Louis 1% earnings tax (residents and nonresidents working there).
MO.no: Same brackets for all filers. Limited deduction for federal income tax paid (TF footnote b; percentage/caps not re-verified). Top rate 4.7% confirmed by 2026 withholding methods (trigger cut not applied). Federal standard deduction amounts (MO 2026 withholding).

MT.no: HB 337 (2025): top rate 5.65% for 2026 (5.4% in 2027); 4.7% bracket widened to $47,500 single / $71,250 HOH / $95,000 MFJ (MT DOR). Treatment of federal tips/overtime deductions not verified. Federal standard deduction (Montana starts from federal taxable income).

NE.no: Brackets from NE DOR 2026 tax calculation schedule. Top rate scheduled 3.99% in 2027 (LB 754). Inflation indexed. $176 personal exemption credit per person.

NH.no: No tax on wages. The interest & dividends tax was repealed for tax periods beginning on/after Jan 1, 2025.

NJ.lo: No local income tax on employees (Newark levies a 1% payroll tax on employers).

NM.no: Federal standard deduction amounts. $4,000 deduction for each dependent except one (in lieu of personal exemption).

NY.lo: New York City resident tax 3.078%-3.876%; Yonkers resident surcharge 16.75% of net NYS tax and 0.5% nonresident earnings tax.
NY.no: Tax benefit recapture applies at higher incomes (top rate applies to all income). OBBBA: FY2027 budget adopts a state exclusion of up to $25,000 of qualified tips for tax years beginning 2026; no state overtime deduction. Dependent exemption only.

ND.no: Bracket thresholds are 2025 indexed amounts per TF (footnote j); 2026 indexed thresholds could not be confirmed. Treatment of federal tips/overtime deductions not verified (they would flow through the federal-taxable-income start unless decoupled). Federal standard deduction (ND starts from federal taxable income).

OH.lo: Municipal income taxes in most cities/villages, ~0.5%-3% (e.g., Columbus and Cleveland 2.5%); many school districts add 0.25%-2%.
OH.no: IMPORTANT: statutory schedule for 2026+ is $0 tax up to $26,050, then $332 PLUS 2.75% of income over $26,050 (ORC 5747.02) - the $332 base is not captured by the bracket array. Same brackets for all filing statuses. Business income taxed separately at 3% after $250k deduction. No standard deduction. Per person: $2,400 if Ohio AGI <= $40,000; $2,150 for $40,001-$80,000; $1,900 for $80,001-$500,000; $0 above $500,000.

OK.no: HB 2764 (2025) consolidated brackets for 2026; further 0.25-pt cuts possible via revenue triggers.

OR.lo: Portland Metro Supportive Housing Services tax 1% of taxable income over $125k single / $200k joint; Multnomah County Preschool for All 1.5% over $125k/$200k plus 1.5% more over $250k/$400k; statewide transit tax 0.1% of wages.
OR.no: Limited subtraction for federal income tax paid (capped, phased out at higher AGI; amount not re-verified). Per Oregon DOR 2026 withholding formulas. Personal exemption credit $263 per person per the 2026 DOR withholding formula (TF table showed $256, the 2025 amount). Not allowed if federal AGI exceeds $100,000 single / $200,000 MFJ.

PA.lo: Local earned income tax (Act 32), typically ~1%-2% combined municipal + school district (higher in some cities, e.g., Pittsburgh 3%); Philadelphia wage tax 3.735% resident / 3.425% nonresident from July 1, 2026 (3.74%/3.43% before); many municipalities also levy a $52/yr Local Services Tax.
PA.no: Flat tax on PA's own classes of income. No standard deduction. No exemptions (Tax Forgiveness credit for low incomes).

RI.no: Same brackets for all filing statuses. H.7127 (2026) millionaire surtax phases in from 2027 (top rate 6.99% 2027 rising to 8.99% 2029) - not in effect for 2026. Phases out between modified federal AGI $261,000 and $290,800. Same $261,000-$290,800 phase-out.

SC.no: Act 110 of 2026 (H.4216), effective TY2026: 1.99% on taxable income under $30,000 and 5.21% above (SCDOR formula: 5.21% x TI - $966); brackets CPI-indexed; future revenue-triggered cuts. TF's Feb-2026 table (0%/3%/6%, $8,350/$16,700) is superseded. Starting point moved to federal AGI and federal std/itemized deductions disallowed, so federal tips/overtime deductions do not flow through. South Carolina Income Adjusted Deduction (SCIAD) replaces federal standard/itemized deductions: $15,000 single/MFS, $22,500 HOH, $30,000 MFJ; reduced proportionally as federal AGI rises from $40,000 to $95,000 (single), $60,000-$142,500 (HOH), $80,000-$190,000 (MFJ), fully gone above. SC dependent exemption (not repealed by Act 110; amount per TF, inflation indexed).

TN.no: No individual income tax (Hall tax on interest/dividends fully repealed from 2021).

UT.no: Flat tax. SB 60 (2026) cut the rate 4.5% -> 4.45% retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 (TF's Feb-2026 table showed 4.5%). Not a deduction: nonrefundable taxpayer tax credit = 6% of the federal standard deduction ($16,100/$32,200) (or itemized deductions less state income tax) plus 6% of dependent exemptions; the whole credit is reduced by 1.3% of income over $18,213 single / $36,426 MFJ (2025 thresholds per TF; 2026 indexed values not confirmed). Dependent exemption $2,111 (per TF) is not deducted from income; it enters the taxpayer credit at 6% (~$127 per dependent) and shares the same phase-out.

VT.no: Brackets/deductions are 2025 indexed amounts (TF footnotes j, n); Vermont had only published TY2025 rate schedules. Filers with federal AGI over $150,000 pay the greater of regular tax or 3% of federal AGI. 2025 amount per TF (2026 not published); +$1,250 per federal age/blind box (2025). 2025 amount per TF.

VA.no: Same brackets for all filing statuses. Virginia Tax: remains $8,750/$17,500 for TY2026; rises to $9,200/$18,400 in 2027.

WA.no: No tax on wages. Capital gains tax on long-term gains: 7% on gains above the annual standard deduction ($278,000 for 2025; 2026 indexed amount not confirmed), plus 2.9% (9.9% total) on gains over $1,000,000 (since 2025). SB 6346 (2026) enacts a 9.9% tax on income over $1 million (incl. wages) starting Jan 1, 2028 - under legal challenge, not in effect for 2026. WA Cares long-term-care premium 0.58% of wages and PFML premiums are payroll deductions, not income tax.

WV.lo: No local income tax (some cities charge flat weekly city service/user fees).
WV.no: SB 392 (signed Mar 31, 2026) cut all rates ~5%, retroactive to Jan 1, 2026 (WV Tax Division schedule). Same brackets for single/MFJ/HOH; MFS brackets are halved. TF's Feb-2026 table (2.22%-4.82%) is superseded. No standard deduction. $2,000 per person.

WI.no: Sliding-scale deduction: phases out starting at $20,119 (single) / $29,039 (MFJ) income, reaching $0 at $136,453 / $159,690 (TF).
